description.narrative: (A) PROJECT OUTCOMES. (A1) Quality of Power. This investment will fund three transmission projects in Peru which will add 224km of new high-voltage lines and increase substation capacity. As such, the investment will contribute to strengthen the national grid and support a higher penetration of renewables in a country that is working to decarbonize its energy matrix - still heavily reliant on fossil fuels (38% of electricity production in 2021). One of the projects is southern Peru - a region with strong renewable resources that is experiencing curtailment. The other two projects are located in the north a low-income isolated region that still relies on diesel for grid stability - and they will allow an increased flow of energy in the Peru-Ecuador interconnection system. The main expected contribution is the improved quality of power supply by adding new transmission capacity, upgrading and modernizing incumbent infrastructure, and increasing the penetration of renewable energy resources to the grid. (A2) Access and Quality of Public Transport. This investment will fund part of Metro Line 6 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The infrastructure investment rate in Brazil has been low in the last decade compared to other EMs, particularly in the transport sector. Existing transport infrastructure has also suffered recently from increasingly frequent adverse climate effects. This project will connect 600,000 daily passengers from low-income suburbs to the city center. Improvements in quality may represent lower travel times (up to 1.5h less than current alternatives), lower accidents through an alternative to road transportation, improved air conditions, and enhanced resilience of public transport infrastructure. (B) MARKET CREATION - Financial Integration. The investment will be structured as a green and sustainability-linked loan, with an innovative social target on access to energy for rural households, contributing to the integration of sustainable finance in Peru and Brazil.

The proposed investment is a 7-year green and sustainability-linked loan (SLL) for up to US$600 million to Acciona Financiacion Filiales S.A. (the Borrower), a wholly owned financing vehicle of Acciona, S.A. (the Sponsor). The loan will finance sustainable infrastructure projects owned by the Sponsor in emerging markets, including but not limited to Peru and Brazil, under Accionas Sustainable Impact Financing Framework. The loan will be linked to sustainability indicators and is part of a broader global partnership between Acciona and IFC to promote sustainable infrastructure in emerging markets.
